subject: TTFT + streaming SLOs — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechx.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: TTFT + streaming SLOs — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what I heard and the asks from your team so we can align next steps: 

Summary of targets you shared
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 150–200 ms for interactive flows (aiming for 150ms at p50, 200ms at p95)
- Throughput: baseline 200 requests/sec average, peaks up to ~800 req/s during market open spikes
- Concurrency: steady 30–50 concurrent streams, burstable to 150 for short windows
- Streaming: prefer Server-Sent Events (SSE) for browser clients; WebSocket optional for mobile apps
- Chunk cadence: typical cadence target ~50–100 ms between chunks for smooth UX; chunk payloads ~128–256 tokens max
- Fallback: acceptable to degrade to non-streaming/long-poll for <5% of calls during overloads

What we need from you to run a focused technical POC
1) A representative sample payload (prompt + metadata + expected avg token output). If possible, include 1–2 worst-case long prompts.
2) Expected distribution of request sizes (p50/p95/p99 tokens) and peak traffic windows (timezones and durations).
3) Confirmation on network topology constraints (e.g., if all traffic must originate from your VPC region us-east-1) and any proxying/agent requirements.
4) Any compliance constraints for the POC (e.g., data residency, log retention).

Next steps I propose
- We’ll spin up a dedicated POC configuration: streaming-enabled endpoint (SSE) with TTFT profiling and telemetry, plus a short harness to replay your sample payloads.
- Redwood will capture TTFT p50/p95/p99, chunk cadence, and end-to-end latency under various concurrency profiles.
- Internal sync: I’ll loop in Vivek (systems lead) and Markus (engineering manager) for capacity planning and quote prep.

Deliverables and timeline
- I’ll send a test harness and a quick configuration doc by EOD tomorrow.
- Proposal for a 3–5 day POC once you sign off on sample payloads and traffic windows.

Attachments: redwood-ttft-profile.pdf (high-level approach), sample_payload.json (example format)

Let me know if anything above is off — happy to adjust. If you’re good with the scope, can we lock a 30–45 minute follow-up tech session next week (I’m flexible Tue/Wed afternoon PT)?

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechx.com>

Cc: FintechX - Engineering <eng@fintechx.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: TTFT + streaming SLOs — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:
- TTFT: goal is 150ms p50, 220ms p95. If p95 creeps over 220ms we want automated throttling/fallback.
- Throughput: baseline 200 rps with two 15-minute windows that can spike up to 800 rps (09:30–09:45 ET and 16:00–16:15 ET).
- Concurrency: target 50 sustained, ability to burst to 150 for up to 20 minutes.
- Streaming: SSE preferred for web. We will test WebSocket later for mobile.
- Chunk cadence: prefer ~75 ms between small chunks; tolerable up to 150 ms.

I attached the sample_payload.json (two prompts — normal + worst-case long). I also confirmed we can host the replay traffic from us-east-1. Compliance: standard SOC2 needs apply; we’ll share the questionnaire later.

—Samir
Director of Integrations | FintechX
samir.patel@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: TTFT + streaming SLOs — post-call recap & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the sample payload and the timing. Next steps from Redwood side:

1) POC setup- We’ll provision a streaming-enabled endpoint in us-east-1 and ship a small test harness (redwood-test-harness.zip) that can replay both payloads at configurable rps/concurrency.
- We’ll instrument TTFT at the edge and at the model runtime so you get p50/p95/p99 split for both first-token and overall response.

2) SLO safety nets
- Default policy: when p95 TTFT exceeds 220ms under load we’ll route non-critical traffic to a lower-cost non-streaming variant and trigger an alert.
- We’ll also test controlled bursts to 150 concurrency to validate graceful degradation.

3) Quote & capacity
- Vivek and Markus — can you confirm an initial sizing and a rough dedicated capacity quote we can present to FintechX? We’ll start with a small reserved buffer to guarantee the TTFT targets during the two daily spike windows.

4) Scheduling
- Samir — I booked Tue Nov 24 10:00 PT for the setup call on my calendar. Invite pending — I’ll send the Meet link once you accept.

Attached: redwood-ttft-profile.pdf, sample_payload.json, redwood-test-harness.zip

I’ll also drop a short Runbook in the Drive (link below) for the POC so your engs can follow the replay steps.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Best,
Marissa
